newsitem.title: UK: Shield says some AFT samples mishandled.
newsitem.headline: Shield says some AFT samples mishandled.

text.p: Shield Diagnostic Group Plc said on Friday that clinical trials carried out in the U.S. linked to its heart attack diagnostic product may have been affected by the mishandling of some samples.

In a statement the company said analysis of data from the U.S. trial of a blood-clotting agent, AFT, "could therefore lead to misleading conclusions." Shares in the company, which hit an all-time high of 928 pence earlier on Friday, plunged 290 pence to 515 pence on the announcement.

Shares in the group have rocketed in recent months amid optimism that its diagnostic test for Activated Factor Twelve, (AFT) will prove to be an accurate predictor of propensity to heart attacks. Immediately after the announcement, Shield shares shed 290 pence ($4.62) -- around half their value -- to stand at 515p before making a modest recovery. Earlier the shares had touched a new year high of 928p.

The company reported initial positive results from the U.S. trial, known as the ARIC trial, and an independent trial in Britain based at st Bartholomew's Hospital, London, earlier this year. Shield said one of the ARIC trial organisers had informed it that "at least some of the samples taken in 1986 have suffered from their handling or storage over the ensuing 10 years," adding that "analysis of data from these samples could therefo lead to misleading conclusions."

The Scottish-based company added that it was "confident in the body of consistent positive data from a number of clinical sites," particularly from St Bartholomew's, and that the timetable for commercial sales of the diagnostic test would not be affected.
The company is to give an update on AFT on March 24. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
